title: Machine marks on AP free responses
statement: Can a machine marker score AP-style short answers and essays reliably enough to award mastery, once calibrated against independently scored responses?
detail: An AP history course's production plan names the case where a response cannot be graded confidently: record it without verified mastery or XP, route low-confidence constructed responses to human review, and calibrate against independently scored AP responses before enabling mastery effects. Its status file lists target-runtime mastery, XP, event and accessibility behaviour as contracted, not run, so no calibration result exists. Until one does, the plan gives a machine score of a free response no power over mastery.
against: Published evidence points both ways: one benchmark found model judges scoring educational responses higher than people and agreeing with them only in part, while a large study found model and human markers of short answers agreeing almost as well as people agree with each other.

evidence.quote: 1. Record the response without verified mastery or XP. 2. Route low-confidence constructed responses to human review. 3. Calibrate against independently scored AP responses before enabling mastery effects.
